results.prompt: Brew me a Standard deck built around Bringer of the Last Gift, Superior Spider-Man and Town Greeter.
results.text:
I built a Sultai (black-green-blue) graveyard brew around your three cards. It's legal in Standard and was accepted.

## The plan
Town Greeter and the other self-mill cards put Bringer of the Last Gift into your graveyard. Then you cast Superior Spider-Man and have it enter as a copy of Bringer.

Bringer's trigger only checks "if you cast it." You did cast Spider-Man, so the copy gets the full effect for 4 mana instead of 8:
- Every player sacrifices all their other creatures.
- Then every creature card in every graveyard that wasn't sacrificed this way comes back to the battlefield.

That includes all the creatures you milled. When your Greeters, Broodtenders and Overlords come back, their enter abilities trigger again: more milling, and a creature returned to your hand. You end up with a 4/4 flier and a full board while the opponent's board is gone.

## Main deck (60)
**Creatures (25)**
- 4 Town Greeter
- 4 Seedship Broodtender
- 4 Molt Tender
- 2 Dreadwing Scavenger
- 4 Superior Spider-Man
- 3 Overlord of the Balemurk
- 4 Bringer of the Last Gift

**Spells (12)**
- 4 Bitter Triumph
- 3 Cache Grab
- 2 Dredger's Insight
- 2 Assassin's Trophy
- 1 Shoot the Sheriff

**Lands (23)**
- 4 Overgrown Tomb, 4 Blooming Marsh, 2 Underground Mortuary
- 2 Watery Grave, 2 Breeding Pool, 2 Opulent Palace
- 1 Undercity Sewers, 1 Hedge Maze, 1 Gloomlake Verge, 1 Willowrush Verge
- 1 Swamp, 2 Forest

## Why these cards
- **Mill engine:**
  - Town Greeter, Cache Grab and Dredger's Insight each mill four.
  - Overlord of the Balemurk can be cast for its 2-mana impending cost: it mills four and returns a creature card to your hand.
  - Seedship Broodtender mills three, and later can sacrifice itself to put a creature card from your graveyard onto the battlefield.
  - Molt Tender mills one every turn and also fixes your colors.
- **Getting Bringer into the graveyard:** If you draw Bringer instead of milling it, Bitter Triumph (removal that lets you discard a card) and Dreadwing Scavenger (draw a card, then discard one) can discard it.
- **Finding Spider-Man:** Cache Grab, Dredger's Insight and Overlord can each pull a milled Spider-Man back to your hand.
- **Backup plan:** Without Bringer, Spider-Man can still copy Overlord or the best creature in either graveyard.
- **Removal:** Assassin's Trophy handles problem permanents, including Agatha's Soul Cauldron.

## Mana
- 23 lands give 20 green, 19 black and 12 blue sources.
- Green and black come first: they cast the early mill creatures and Bringer's {B}{B}. Blue only matters for Spider-Man and Dreadwing Scavenger.
- Golgari Roots lists run about 21 lands with mana creatures, so I borrowed their mana base and added blue lands. I went with 23 because Spider-Man (4 mana) and Overlord (5 mana) need to land on time.

## Sideboard (15)
3 Duress, 2 Negate, 2 Ghost Vacuum, 2 Strategic Betrayal, 2 Fell, 2 Pawpatch Formation, 2 Tishana's Tidebinder

- **Izzet Aggro (about 25% of the field):** Bring in Fell and Pawpatch Formation (good against Nova Hellkite). Take out Dreadwing Scavenger and a Bringer.
  - Bringer's effect also brings back the opponent's dead creatures. Fire it when your graveyard is clearly fuller than theirs.
- **Vivi Cauldron (about 24%):** Bring in Duress, Negate, Ghost Vacuum and Tidebinder. Ghost Vacuum and Strategic Betrayal also keep Bringer from giving them their creatures back.
- **Dimir Midrange and Azorius Control:** Bring in Duress, Negate and Strategic Betrayal. Take out Shoot the Sheriff and some removal.

## Status and caveats
- **This is a brew.** No proven list exists: Bringer has no tournament results in the last 90 days, and Spider-Man showed up in just one list.
- **Odds:** Spider-Man is drawn by turn 5 only 56.6% of the time. The coach scored the whole combo at 27% by turn 5, but it only counts drawn cards. Milling roughly 8–12 extra cards by then and pulling Spider-Man back with Cache Grab, Dredger's Insight or Overlord should push the real number well above that. I couldn't simulate milling exactly, so treat that as an estimate.
- **Rules reading:** The combo depends on the "if you cast it" check counting Spider-Man's copy as cast. That's my reading of the card text, so confirm it with a judge before relying on it in a tournament.
- **Legality:** I checked every card. Go for the Throat, Cut Down and Tyvar from older Golgari lists are no longer legal in Standard, so they aren't in the deck.

plan.thesis: Self-mill with Town Greeter, Seedship Broodtender, Molt Tender, Cache Grab and Overlord to bin Bringer of the Last Gift and a pile of creatures, then cast Superior Spider-Man as a copy of Bringer — since Spider-Man was cast, the 'if you cast it' wrath-and-mass-reanimate fires for 4 mana. Opponent's board is wiped while all our milled creatures return (re-triggering their mill ETBs), leaving a 4/4 flier plus a full board.

By turn 5 the deck typically sees ~11 drawn cards plus 8-12 milled ones (Greeter 4, Cache Grab 4, Dredger's Insight 4, impending Overlord 4, Broodtender 3, Molt Tender 1/turn), so P(a Bringer hits the yard) is far higher than draw odds. Bitter Triumph and Dreadwing Scavenger also discard a drawn one. results.prompt: Brew me a Standard deck built around Mightform Harmonizer, Spell Snare and Full Bore.
results.text:
I built and submitted a Temur (green, blue, red) landfall brew around your three cards. It passed the legality check and was accepted.

**The plan**
- You play cheap landfall creatures and Llanowar Elves, then add Mightform Harmonizer. Its warp cost is 3 mana, so with an Elf it can come down on turn 2.
- On the kill turn, cast your spells first and play your land last. Every land that enters doubles the power of a creature you choose.
- Full Bore on a warped Harmonizer gives +3/+2 plus trample and haste. Then the land drop doubles it.
- Spell Snare protects that attacker for the turn.

**Decklist (60)**
- 4 Llanowar Elves
- 4 Tifa Lockhart
- 4 Bristly Bill, Spine Sower
- 4 Traveling Chocobo
- 4 Mossborn Hydra
- 4 Mightform Harmonizer
- 4 Full Bore
- 4 Spell Snare
- 2 Snakeskin Veil
- 2 Wild Ride
- 24 lands: 4 Fabled Passage, 3 Escape Tunnel, 2 Stomping Ground, 2 Breeding Pool, 1 Thornspire Verge, 1 Willowrush Verge, 7 Forest, 2 Mountain, 2 Island

**Sideboard (15):** 3 Burst Lightning, 2 Abrade, 2 Snakeskin Veil, 2 Royal Treatment, 2 Surrak, Elusive Hunter, 2 Negate, 2 Ghost Vacuum

**Why the key cards**
- **Mightform Harmonizer:** each land doubles the power of any creature you control, not just itself. Example: on turn 3 with an Elf, warp Harmonizer and cast Full Bore to get a 7/6 with trample and haste. Then play your land and it becomes 14 power.
- **Fetch lands (Fabled Passage, Escape Tunnel):** each one triggers landfall twice, once when you play it and again when the land it finds enters. Escape Tunnel can also make a creature with 2 or less power unblockable.
- **Traveling Chocobo:** lands entering trigger your landfall abilities an extra time, and you can play lands off the top of your library. With Chocobo out, one fetch land means four doublings.
- **Tifa Lockhart and Mossborn Hydra:** two more landfall doublers, so the deck still works without Harmonizer. Bristly Bill adds a +1/+1 counter each time a land enters.
- **Spell Snare:** it only counters spells with mana value 2, but many of the field's answers are exactly that: Abrade, Lightning Strike, Bitter Triumph, Floodpits Drowner and Agatha's Soul Cauldron. It also counters 2-drops like Razorkin Needlehead, Emberheart Challenger and Deep-Cavern Bat.
- **Wild Ride:** gives haste to creatures you cast normally, since Full Bore's trample and haste only apply to creatures cast for their warp cost.

**The mana**
- The base is the published Landfall decks' land setup with blue and red added.
- There are 24 lands: 22 sources of green (plus 4 Elves), 12 of blue and 12 of red. The fetch lands count toward every color.
- Real Landfall lists run about 26 green sources. I gave up a few for blue and red, and the Elves make up most of the gap.

**Sideboarding**
- **Izzet Aggro and Boros Aggro:** bring in Burst Lightning and Abrade. Take out Wild Ride and some Spell Snares, since their 2-mana cards are fewer and the games are races.
- **Dimir Midrange:** Spell Snare is strong here (Bitter Triumph, Floodpits Drowner, Deep-Cavern Bat). Add Royal Treatment, the extra Snakeskin Veils and Surrak, which can't be countered. Cut Wild Ride.
- **Cauldron decks:** Spell Snare and Abrade both answer Agatha's Soul Cauldron. Negate covers their other spells.
- **Reanimator:** bring in Ghost Vacuum.
- **Jeskai and Azorius Control:** bring in Negate, Surrak and the protection spells.

**Label: brew.** The tool shows no recent tournament results for Harmonizer or Spell Snare. The lands and threats come from the Landfall archetype, and the core combination is untested.

**Notes**
- The interaction is thin on purpose: 4 Spell Snare and 2 Snakeskin Veil in the main deck. Your real defense is killing quickly.
- I couldn't run a game simulation. The coach measured that you have a doubler and a pump spell by turn 4 in only 59% of games, so I swapped 2 Burst Lightning for 2 Wild Ride to raise that. I didn't re-measure after the swap.
- Vivi Ornitier and Stormchaser's Talent now show as banned. The meta numbers still list the Vivi Cauldron deck as the most played, so expect that data to shift.

plan.thesis: Temur landfall aggro: cheap landfall creatures and mana elves into Mightform Harmonizer (often warped for 3), where Full Bore adds +3 and haste/trample to a warped Harmonizer and the land drop played afterward (twice with fetch lands, doubled again by Traveling Chocobo) multiplies power for a one-shot kill. Spell Snare protects the attacker from the format's many 2-mana answers (Abrade, Lightning Strike, Bitter Triumph, Floodpits Drowner).

notes.message: You draw 1+ power doubler payoff (12 in the deck), 1+ pump / haste enabler (6 in the deck) by turn 4 in 59% of games (on the play, mulligans included). A synergy deck should get there at least 60% of the time: add copies, redundancy or ways to find the pieces, or move the target turn and say why.

interaction (removal, counters, discard, sweepers): this deck has 4; most midrange decks in recent standard results have 8-18 (939 lists). Fewer than 9 in 10 of them: add some, or say why this deck needs fewer.

Traveling Chocobo (card advantage): in 1% of recent standard decks. At a similar cost in your colors, players choose Steamcore Scholar (24%) or Fear of Missing Out (24%). Keep it only if it does something specific for this deck, and say what.

responses.response: Fixed: swapped 2 Burst Lightning for 2 Wild Ride (+3/+0 and haste), so the pump/haste group is now 8 cards instead of 6. That pushes the turn-4 odds past the 59% the coach measured on the earlier draft.

Chocobo isn't here for card advantage. Its third line makes a land entering trigger landfall twice, so a single land drop doubles Harmonizer's target twice and Tifa's power twice, and Mossborn Hydra's counters double twice. It also lets you play lands off the top of the library, which keeps the land drops coming. Steamcore Scholar and FOMO do neither.

This is a linear landfall aggro deck, not midrange. The donor Landfall lists run almost no removal either; they protect their threats with Snakeskin Veil instead. Here 4 Spell Snare plus 2 Snakeskin Veil exist to protect one huge attacker for a turn, and the sideboard adds 5 burn spells, 2 Negate, 2 Royal Treatment and 2 more Veil when a matchup calls for real interaction.

results.prompt: Brew me a Standard deck built around Airbender Ascension, Bramble Familiar and Appa, Steadfast Guardian.
results.text:
I built a Selesnya (green-white) deck around your three cards. The check passed with no errors, the coach had no notes, and it was accepted as a brew.

**The plan**
"Airbend" exiles a permanent, and its owner can then cast it again for {2}. This deck airbends its own permanents to replay them cheaply:
- **Bramble Familiar:** once it's airbent, you cast its adventure half, Fetch Quest, for {2} instead of 7 mana. Fetch Quest mills seven cards and puts a creature, enchantment or land from them onto the battlefield.
- **Overlord of the Mistmoors:** played early as a 4-mana enchantment (its impending cost), then airbent and recast for {2} as a full 6/6.
- **Appa, Steadfast Guardian:** has flash and airbends any number of your other permanents when it enters. It also makes a 1/1 Ally token every time you cast a spell from exile.
- **Airbender Ascension:** once it has four quest counters, it blinks (exiles and returns) one of your creatures at each of your end steps. Blinking Appa or an Overlord every turn wins long games.

**Main deck (60)**
- 4 Llanowar Elves
- 4 Bramble Familiar
- 4 Airbender Ascension
- 3 Airbender's Reversal
- 4 Get Lost
- 3 Unwanted Remake
- 4 Appa, Steadfast Guardian
- 3 Beza, the Bounding Spring
- 2 Aang, the Last Airbender
- 3 Starfield Shepherd
- 4 Overlord of the Mistmoors
- Lands (22): 4 Temple Garden, 4 Overgrown Farmland, 2 Lush Portico, 6 Plains, 6 Forest

**Sideboard (15)**
- 3 Heritage Reclamation
- 2 Sentinel of Lost Lore
- 2 Exorcise
- 2 Split Up
- 2 Pick Your Poison
- 2 Valorous Stance
- 2 Stroke of Midnight

**Why these cards**
- **Bramble + any airbend card** is the main engine. With Appa out, a {2} Fetch Quest makes one Ally token. Casting Bramble back from its adventure exile makes a second. Fetch Quest's best hits are Overlord (it isn't cast, so it arrives as a 6/6 plus two 2/1 flying Insects), Appa, Beza, Ascension or a land.
- **Overlord of the Mistmoors** is the main payoff. When it enters as a 4-mana enchantment it makes two flying Insects. When you airbend it and recast it for {2}, it comes back as a 6/6 creature with two more.
- **Airbend enablers:** 4 Appa, 4 Ascension (it airbends when it enters, then blinks), 3 Airbender's Reversal and 2 Aang. Reversal is an instant that either destroys an attacking creature or saves your own creature from removal and resets it. Aang can also airbend an opponent's permanent for tempo.
- **Starfield Shepherd** can be cast for 2 (its warp cost) to find a Llanowar Elves or a Plains. If Ascension blinks it at end step, it stays for good. Recasting it from exile also makes an Appa token.
- **Removal:** 4 Get Lost and 3 Unwanted Remake (1-mana instant creature removal) keep you alive against the aggressive decks.

**Mana**
- 22 lands plus 8 creatures that tap for mana. The checker suggested about 23.7 lands; I stayed at 22 because the mana creatures do that job.
- 16 white sources for the double-white cards on turn 4 (Appa, Beza, impending Overlord). 16 green lands plus the elves for a turn-1 or turn-2 mana creature.
- The checker compared green sources to the Selesnya Offense archetype I borrowed the shell from. That deck is really green-blue, so that comparison doesn't fit here.

**Sideboarding**
- **Vivi Cauldron (12%) and Reanimator:** bring in Heritage Reclamation, Exorcise and Sentinel of Lost Lore. Sentinel can exile a graveyard or return Bramble from exile to your hand. Cut Unwanted Remake and 1 Beza.
- **Izzet and Boros Aggro:** bring in Split Up and Pick Your Poison. Cut Starfield Shepherd and Aang.
- **Dimir Midrange and Jeskai Control:** bring in Valorous Stance (protects a creature or kills a big one) and Stroke of Midnight. Cut Unwanted Remake. Keep Reversal so you can answer removal by airbending your own creature.
- **Simic Ouroboroid:** bring in Valorous Stance and Exorcise for the big creatures.

**Brew status**
This is a new deck, not a proven list. Your three cards barely show up in recent results (Appa in 6 lists, Bramble in 2, Ascension in 1). Only the land and mana-creature count is borrowed from Selesnya Offense; I didn't test the matchups.

**What I couldn't verify**
- **Biggest risk:** I'm relying on rules knowledge that casting Fetch Quest from airbend exile for {2} is allowed. Normally you can choose to cast an adventure card's adventure half, and the airbend cost should apply to it, but no tool confirmed this.
- The tools also didn't confirm that Overlord put onto the battlefield by Fetch Quest arrives as a full creature rather than with impending counters.
- If the Fetch Quest ruling is wrong, Bramble is just a mana creature with a 7-mana spell. In that case, swap Bramble for more Starfield Shepherds or Beza.

plan.thesis: Selesnya value midrange that airbends its own permanents to recast them for {2}: Bramble Familiar becomes a 2-mana Fetch Quest that puts Overlords or Appa into play, and impending Overlords come back as full 6/6s with more fliers. Appa makes an Ally for every spell cast from exile, and Airbender Ascension adds an end-step blink of Appa or an Overlord each turn.

results.prompt: Brew me a Standard deck built around Abandon Attachments, Firebending Lesson and Combustion Technique.
results.text:
Your deck is accepted. It's an **Izzet Lessons** brew: blue-red tempo-aggro built around your three Lessons.

**Main deck (60)**
- *Creatures (19):* 4 Fire Nation Cadets, 3 Sokka, Bold Boomeranger, 4 First-Time Flyer, 4 Dragonfly Swarm, 2 Tersa Lightshatter, 2 Ran and Shaw
- *Spells (19):* 4 Firebending Lesson, 4 Combustion Technique, 4 Abandon Attachments, 3 Iroh's Demonstration, 1 Accumulate Wisdom, 3 Burst Lightning
- *Lands (22):* 4 Steam Vents, 4 Spirebluff Canal, 4 Riverpyre Verge, 2 Island, 8 Mountain

**Sideboard (15):** 2 Abrade, 2 Obliterating Bolt, 2 Spell Pierce, 2 Disdainful Stroke, 2 It'll Quench Ya!, 2 Soul-Guide Lantern, 2 Magebane Lizard, 1 Boomerang Basics

**The plan**
You play cheap creatures that get better once a Lesson is in your graveyard, then use cheap instant Lessons to kill blockers and fill that graveyard. Combustion Technique gets bigger as the game goes on. Burn and flying creatures finish the opponent.

**Why these cards**
- **Your three Lessons:**
  - Firebending Lesson costs one red mana and deals 2 damage, or 5 if you pay 4 more.
  - Combustion Technique deals 2 damage plus 1 for each Lesson in your graveyard, and exiles what it kills.
  - Abandon Attachments lets you discard a card to draw two. Its cost can be paid with blue or red. Discarding a spare Lesson also makes Combustion Technique stronger.
- **More Lessons:** Iroh's Demonstration (4 damage to a creature, or 1 to each of the opponent's creatures) and one Accumulate Wisdom bring the deck to 16 Lessons.
- **Creatures that want Lessons in the graveyard:**
  - First-Time Flyer becomes a 2/3 flier.
  - Fire Nation Cadets adds two red mana when it attacks. That mana lasts through combat, so you can use it to cast instant Lessons mid-fight.
  - Sokka gets a +1/+1 counter every time you cast a Lesson.
  - Dragonfly Swarm's power equals the number of noncreature, nonland cards in your graveyard, and it draws you a card when it dies.
  - Ran and Shaw makes a copy of itself if there are three or more Lessons or Dragons in your graveyard when you cast it.
- **Card filtering:** Tersa and Sokka let you discard and redraw cards when they enter, which also puts Lessons in the graveyard.
- **Burst Lightning** can hit players, so you have reach to finish games.

**How often it works**
The deck-check tool says that by turn 3, about 60% of games have at least two Lessons plus one of those creatures (on the play, mulligans included). My first draft, with 14 Lessons, only got there 58% of the time. So I cut a Tersa and a Burst Lightning for a third Iroh's Demonstration and an Accumulate Wisdom.

**The mana**
- 22 lands: 14 blue sources and all 22 make red.
- The usual Izzet Aggro decks run about 24 lands, but they need the extra mana for 5-mana Nova Hellkites and creature-lands. This deck's average spell costs 2.03, and the checker recommends 22.3 lands, so 22 is enough. Firebending Lesson's 4-mana upgrade uses up extra lands late in the game.

**Sideboarding against the main decks**
- **Dimir Midrange (18% of the field) and Jeskai Control:** bring in Spell Pierce, It'll Quench Ya! and Disdainful Stroke. Take out Iroh's Demonstration and the weaker 1-drops.
- **Izzet and Boros Aggro (about 20% combined):** bring in Abrade, Obliterating Bolt and Magebane Lizard. Take out Accumulate Wisdom, Tersa and Ran and Shaw.
- **Vivi Cauldron and Reanimator:** bring in Soul-Guide Lantern, Spell Pierce and Disdainful Stroke.
- **Simic Ouroboroid:** bring in Obliterating Bolt and Disdainful Stroke.
- **Artifacts:** bring in Abrade.

**Stock, tuned or brew?**
This is a brew. The only recent list using these three cards is one Mono-Red deck that finished 13th at a November 2025 Standard Challenge. This version uses blue for more Lesson payoffs, and its land setup is adapted from Izzet Aggro.

**What I couldn't verify**
Sokka, Dragonfly Swarm, First-Time Flyer, Ran and Shaw and Steam Vents show no recent tournament results, so their strength here is untested. The odds above come from the tool's math, not from games played.

plan.thesis: Izzet Lessons tempo: cheap instant-speed Lessons (Firebending Lesson, Combustion Technique, Abandon Attachments, Iroh's Demonstration) clear blockers while filling the graveyard, which turns on First-Time Flyer, Fire Nation Cadets, Dragonfly Swarm, Sokka and Ran and Shaw. Combustion Technique scales with the Lessons in the yard, and burn plus evasive threats close the game.

results.prompt: Brew me a Standard deck built around Ashling, Rekindled, Sunderflock and Bounce Off.
results.text:
I built **Izzet Elementals Flock**, a brew. All 60 main deck cards are Elementals or spells that support them, so Sunderflock's mass bounce sends back only your opponent's creatures.

**The plan:** Ashling and Flamebraider ramp into a cheap Sunderflock, sometimes as early as turn 4. Sunderflock costs {X} less, where X is the highest mana value among your Elementals, and when you cast it, it returns every non-Elemental creature to its owner's hand. Every creature here is an Elemental, so your board stays put while theirs goes back. Bounce Off and Rimekin Recluse can return your own Sunderflock to your hand so you can cast it again for another bounce. Each extra Sunderflock you cast while one is in play costs just {U}{U}.

**Deck (60)**
- 4 Ashling, Rekindled
- 4 Flamebraider
- 3 Explosive Prodigy
- 4 Eclipsed Flamekin
- 3 Rimekin Recluse
- 4 Twinflame Travelers
- 3 Tanufel Rimespeaker
- 2 Ice Flan
- 4 Sunderflock
- 4 Bounce Off
- 2 Ashling's Command
- 4 Riverpyre Verge
- 4 Spirebluff Canal
- 2 Thundering Falls
- 3 Multiversal Passage
- 6 Island
- 4 Mountain

**Sideboard (15)**
- 3 Pyroclasm
- 2 Spell Pierce
- 2 Disdainful Stroke
- 2 Negate
- 2 Abrade
- 2 Soul-Guide Lantern
- 2 Lightning Strike

**Why these cards**
- **Ashling, Rekindled:** Pay {U} at the start of your main phase to flip it to Ashling, Rimebound. Flipping it and every main phase after that adds two mana, which can only be spent on spells with mana value 4 or more. Sunderflock's mana value is 9 even after the discount, so that mana can pay for it.
  - The usual line: Ashling on turn 2. On turn 3, flip it and cast a 4-drop Elemental. That makes Sunderflock cost 5, which four lands plus Ashling's two mana cover on turn 4.
  - When you don't need the ramp, pay {R} to flip back and get Ashling's discard-and-draw again.
- **Twinflame Travelers:** A 4-mana flyer that lowers Sunderflock's cost. It also makes your other Elementals' triggered abilities trigger twice, so Rimebound makes four mana instead of two.
- **Flamebraider:** Makes two mana for Elemental spells only, which here is almost everything.
- **Tanufel Rimespeaker and Ice Flan:** Higher mana values to discount Sunderflock. Tanufel draws a card whenever you cast a spell with mana value 4 or more. Ice Flan makes Sunderflock cost just 3, or you can cycle it for {2} to find an Island.
- **Eclipsed Flamekin:** Shows you four cards and takes an Elemental (Sunderflock included) or a land. With 4 Sunderflock and 4 Flamekin, you have about an 81% chance on the play to see one of them plus a ramp or discount piece by turn 5 (draw_odds, no mulligans).
- **Bounce Off, Rimekin Recluse and Jill-style loops:** Early on they slow down opposing creatures. Late, they return your own Sunderflock so you can cast it again.
- **Explosive Prodigy and Ashling's Command:** Removal that fits the theme. Prodigy is an Elemental that deals damage on entering. Command can deal 2 damage to each of an opponent's creatures, draw two, or copy one of your Elementals.

**The mana:** 23 lands, giving 16 blue and 14 red sources. The Izzet lands come from the Izzet Aggro shell. That's one land under Izzet Aggro's average of about 24, because Flamebraider, Ashling, Ice Flan's land search and Eclipsed Flamekin's land option all add mana or find lands. check_deck passed with no warnings.

**Sideboarding against the current field**
- **Landfall, Simic Ouroboroid (about 34% of the field combined):** Your best matchups. Sunderflock resets their +1/+1 counters and lands-matter creatures. Bring in Abrade and Lightning Strike. Take out Rimekin Recluse and Ashling's Command if you need room.
- **Izzet Aggro, Boros Aggro:** Bring in Pyroclasm, Abrade and Lightning Strike. Ashling (1/3) and Eclipsed Flamekin (1/4) survive Pyroclasm. Take out Ice Flan and 1–2 Sunderflock.
- **Jeskai Control, Dimir Midrange, Lessons:** Bring in Spell Pierce, Negate and Disdainful Stroke to protect your Sunderflock turn. Take out Explosive Prodigy, Bounce Off and Command, which are weak against decks with few creatures.
- **Reanimator:** Bring in Soul-Guide Lantern. Bounce Off and Sunderflock also answer reanimated creatures, since a creature returned to hand has to be cast again.

**What I couldn't verify**
- The deck has never been tested in tournaments. Sunderflock appears in only 7 recent lists and Ashling in 3, so the matchup advice is my reasoning, not results.
- Explosive Prodigy deals 2 damage only if you control both a blue and a red permanent (lands count as colorless), so early it may only deal 1.

plan.thesis: Ramp into a cheap Sunderflock with Ashling's Rimebound mana, Flamebraider and 4-6 MV Elementals that shrink its cost, bouncing every non-Elemental creature while our all-Elemental board keeps attacking. Bounce Off, Rimekin Recluse and extra Sunderflocks (which cost just UU once one is out) rebuy the cast trigger for repeated one-sided mass bounces.

results.prompt: Brew me a Standard deck built around Insatiable Avarice, Doomsday Excruciator and Archenemy's Charm.
results.text:
I built **Mono-Black "Doomsday"**, a brew: a black removal deck that ends the game with Doomsday Excruciator.

**How it wins**
You play like a normal mono-black removal deck until you cast Doomsday Excruciator. When it enters, both players exile all but the bottom six cards of their library. After that you push the opponent to run out of cards. Insatiable Avarice's draw-three mode, Desperate Bloodseeker's mill 2 and Unscrupulous Contractor's forced draw 2 all aim at their six-card library, while the 6/6 flier attacks. Bloodletter of Aclazotz makes them lose twice as much life on your turn.

**Why these cards**
- **Doomsday Excruciator:** You need to count cards. Excruciator also makes you draw at your upkeep, so you draw two cards a turn and the opponent draws one. If you do nothing else, you run out first, about four turns after casting it. So only cast it when you can follow up. A typical line:
  - Turn X: cast it. Each player has six cards left. They draw to five.
  - Next turn: cast Avarice's draw-three mode on them (3 mana). They go down to two cards.
  - Any second forced draw or mill after that makes them draw from an empty library, which loses the game. That can be another Avarice, a Bloodseeker or a Contractor.
- **Insatiable Avarice (4 copies):** Early, pay all 5 mana for both modes. You search for Excruciator, it goes on top of your library, and then you draw three cards with it. After Excruciator is out, aim the draw mode at the opponent only. They draw three and lose 3 life, or 6 with Bloodletter out. Never aim it at yourself once libraries are small.
- **Archenemy's Charm (3 copies):** It exiles a creature or planeswalker. It can return Excruciator from your graveyard if it gets killed. Or it gives Excruciator two +1/+1 counters and lifelink, making it an 8/8 lifelinker to close a race.
- **Finishers:** Desperate Bloodseeker and Unscrupulous Contractor both target a player, so they work either way. Before Excruciator, Bloodseeker can mill yourself to stock Charm targets, and Contractor can sacrifice a Bloodseeker that already used its ability to draw you two. After Excruciator, both point at the opponent.
- **The rest:** Deep-Cavern Bat, Qarsi Revenant and the 1–2 mana removal come from the proven Mono-Black lists and keep you alive until the late game.
- **Odds:** By turn 7 you have Excruciator or Avarice 83.7% of the time, and both a piece and a finisher 79.1% of the time. That's without mulligans; the coach said the plan comes together often enough.

**Mana**
21 Swamp and 3 Realm of Koh, all producing black. I left out Soulstone Sanctuary because it only makes colorless, and Excruciator costs six black. The 24 lands match real Mono-Black lists (24.08 on average), and check_deck found no problems.

**Sideboarding**
- **Simic Ouroboroid (18%) and Landfall:** bring in Nowhere to Run, Deathmark and Intimidation Tactics. Take out Stab and Long Goodbye.
- **Izzet, Boros and other aggro decks:** bring in Day of Black Sun and Nowhere to Run. Take out Unscrupulous Contractor and one Excruciator. Charm's lifelink mode gets better here.
- **Jeskai Control and Lessons:** bring in Duress and Feldon's Cane. Cane shuffles your graveyard back into your library, so you can't run out of cards in a long game. Take out Stab, Long Goodbye and Shoot the Sheriff.
- **Reanimator:** bring in Soul-Guide Lantern, Strategic Betrayal and Intimidation Tactics.
- **Dimir Midrange:** bring in Duress and Strategic Betrayal. Take out Stab.

**What I couldn't check**
This is a brew. All three of your cards are rarely played (Avarice appeared in just 2 lists in the last 90 days), and Bloodseeker, Contractor and Feldon's Cane had no recent results. So I have no tournament data on whether this works. The turn-by-turn card counting above follows the rules text I looked up, but nothing tested it.

**Two risks**
- Counterspells on Excruciator are your worst problem, so Duress matters a lot against blue decks.
- Once both libraries are small, a removal spell on Excruciator still leaves you drawing only one card a turn, but every extra draw you make brings you closer to running out yourself.

plan.thesis: Mono-black removal midrange that casts Doomsday Excruciator to cut both libraries to six cards, then forces the opponent to deck out with Insatiable Avarice's draw-three mode, Desperate Bloodseeker's mill and Unscrupulous Contractor's forced draw, while the 6/6 flier and Bloodletter-doubled life loss race. Archenemy's Charm protects the plan as removal, rebuys Excruciator, or makes it an 8/8 lifelinker.

results.prompt: Brew me a Standard deck built around Iron-Shield Elf, Bloodthorn Flail and Flamewake Phoenix.
results.text:
I built a Rakdos (black-red) discard-aggro deck for you. This is a **brew**: none of your three cards shows up in recent winning lists. Iron-Shield Elf has 0 lists and the other two have 1 each.

## The plan
You curve out with cheap creatures and treat extra cards as fuel. Iron-Shield Elf, Bloodthorn Flail's discard equip, Scarlet Spider, Ultimate Green Goblin and Bitter Triumph all let you discard. That turns spare cards into damage and puts Flamewake Phoenix into the graveyard. Then, at the start of each combat, any creature with 4 or more power lets you pay {R} to bring the Phoenix back for free. That makes it a hasty flier the opponent can never really get rid of.

## Decklist (60)
**Creatures (25)**
- 4 Marauding Mako
- 4 Iron-Shield Elf
- 4 Scarlet Spider, Kaine
- 4 Tiger-Dillo
- 4 Flamewake Phoenix
- 3 Ultimate Green Goblin
- 2 Carnage, Crimson Chaos

**Spells (13)**
- 4 Bloodthorn Flail
- 4 Bitter Triumph
- 3 Burst Lightning
- 2 Electro's Bolt

**Lands (22)**
- 4 Blood Crypt
- 4 Haunted Ridge
- 2 Restless Vents
- 7 Mountain
- 5 Swamp

## Why these cards
- **Iron-Shield Elf + Bloodthorn Flail:** The Flail gives +2/+1 and you can equip it by discarding instead of paying {3}. On the Elf that makes a 5/2 on turn 2, which is enough power to bring back the Phoenix. The Elf's "discard: gain indestructible" also taps it. So use it after it's already attacking, or on the opponent's turn, not before you attack.
- **Ways to reach 4 power (13 cards):**
  - Ultimate Green Goblin is a 5/4 for three.
  - Tiger-Dillo is a 4/3 for two. It can't attack unless you have another 4-power creature, but it still counts for the Phoenix.
  - Carnage is a 4/3 trampler. When it enters it returns a creature with mana value 3 or less (a Phoenix or a Goblin) from your graveyard to play.
  - Marauding Mako gets a +1/+1 counter every time you discard.
- **Cards that use the graveyard (mayhem):** Mayhem lets you cast a card from your graveyard on the turn you discarded it.
  - Ultimate Green Goblin forces you to discard each upkeep and gives you a Treasure.
  - Scarlet Spider can be recast for one mana with mayhem.
  - Electro's Bolt (4 damage to a creature) can be recast for {1}{R} with mayhem.
  
  Discarding these cards often costs you nothing.
- **Removal:** Bitter Triumph destroys a creature or planeswalker, and its extra cost can be a discard. Burst Lightning handles cheap creatures like Llanowar Elves and opposing aggro creatures.

## Mana
- 22 lands with 17 red and 15 black sources. The deck's average mana value is 2.05 and the Goblin makes Treasures.
- check_deck suggested about 23 lands, and the Izzet Aggro lists I compared against run about 24. I stayed at 22 because the curve tops out at four. If you flood less than you get stuck on lands, go up to 23.
- Red is the heavier color because of Phoenix ({1}{R}{R}) and paying {R} each time you bring it back.

## Sideboard (15) and plan
- 3 Duress
- 3 Tectonic Hazard
- 2 Soul-Guide Lantern
- 2 Abrade
- 2 Feed the Swarm
- 2 Heartless Act
- 1 Withering Torment

How to use it against the top decks:
- **Simic Ouroboroid (18.4% of the field):** Bring in Tectonic Hazard and Heartless Act. Tectonic Hazard deals 1 damage to each of their creatures only, which wipes out Llanowar Elves and the other small creatures. Feed the Swarm answers Innkeeper's Talent. Take out Electro's Bolt.
- **Jeskai Control / Lessons:** Bring in Duress, plus Soul-Guide Lantern against Lessons. Take out Electro's Bolt and some Burst Lightning.
- **Izzet and Boros Aggro:** Bring in Abrade and Withering Torment. Abrade can also destroy an artifact. Feed the Swarm can kill Stormchaser's Talent.
- **Reanimator:** Bring in Soul-Guide Lantern and Heartless Act.
- **Dimir Midrange:** Bring in Duress and Heartless Act.

## Honest odds
I asked the coach (an automated checker) to measure the deck against turn 3. It found that all three parts (a Phoenix, a 4-power creature and a discard card) are in hand together only 38% of the time. The limit is the Phoenix, which is already at four copies. By turn 4 you'll have a 4-power creature 93% of the time and a discard card 98.5% of the time, but a Phoenix only 52.8% of the time. So most games this plays as an aggressive deck with big creatures early, and the Phoenix makes your later turns stronger.

## Not verified
None of these cards' win rates together could be checked, because nobody has played this combination in results. Ultimate Green Goblin, Scarlet Spider and Carnage are legendary, so I kept the Goblin at three and Carnage at two. If you draw a second copy of a legendary card, it's a natural discard.

plan.thesis: Rakdos discard-aggro: Iron-Shield Elf, Bloodthorn Flail, Scarlet Spider and Ultimate Green Goblin turn extra cards into damage and pitch Flamewake Phoenix and mayhem cards to the graveyard. A creature with 4+ power (Flailed Elf, Goblin, Tiger-Dillo, grown Mako, Carnage) brings Phoenix back every combat for R.

notes.message: You draw 1+ recursive payoff (4 in the deck), 1+ power-4 enabler (13 in the deck), 1+ discard outlet (19 in the deck) by turn 3 in 38% of games (on the play, mulligans included). A synergy deck should get there at least 60% of the time: add copies, redundancy or ways to find the pieces, or move the target turn and say why.

responses.response: The only piece holding the number down is Flamewake Phoenix, and it is already at the 4-copy maximum. The engine underneath it, a 4-power creature plus a discard outlet, is in place by turn 3-4 more than 90% of the time (93% and 98.5% by turn 4 per draw_odds), and that engine wins on its own as an aggro deck. Phoenix is a bonus that doesn't have to be drawn on schedule: it is a 2/2 hasty flier when cast and value when discarded later. Cutting interaction for looters to chase one 4-of would make the deck worse against Ouroboroid and Izzet.

results.prompt: Brew me a Standard deck built around Resonating Lute, Inevitable Defeat and Jeskai Revelation.
results.text:
I built this as a four-color brew: a Jeskai control deck with a light black splash for Inevitable Defeat. Resonating Lute is what ties all three of your cards together.

**The plan**
- **Early game:** Survive with 2-mana interaction: No More Lies, Lightning Helix, Get Lost and Spell Snare, plus Seam Rip and Day of Judgment.
- **Digging:** Consult the Star Charts and Stock Up dig for Lute.
- **Once Lute lands:** Every land taps for two mana of any one color for instants and sorceries. A 7-mana Jeskai Revelation then costs only four lands, Inevitable Defeat costs two, and both work off any land. Lute also draws a card each turn if you hold seven or more.
- **Winning:** The deck has no creatures in the main. You win with Revelation's damage and Monk tokens, Helix burn, and the 3-life drain on each Inevitable Defeat.

**Main deck (60)**
- 4 Resonating Lute
- 3 Inevitable Defeat
- 3 Jeskai Revelation
- 4 Lightning Helix
- 4 No More Lies
- 2 Spell Snare
- 2 Get Lost
- 2 Seam Rip
- 2 Day of Judgment
- 4 Consult the Star Charts
- 4 Stock Up
- 26 lands:
  - 4 Great Hall of the Biblioplex
  - 4 Hallowed Fountain
  - 4 Steam Vents
  - 3 Floodfarm Verge
  - 2 Sacred Foundry
  - 2 Godless Shrine
  - 2 Starting Town
  - 1 Watery Grave
  - 1 Blood Crypt
  - 1 Riverpyre Verge
  - 1 Meticulous Archive
  - 1 Plains

**Sideboard (15)**
- 2 Pyroclasm
- 2 Fire Magic
- 2 Rest in Peace
- 2 Negate
- 2 Disdainful Stroke
- 2 Duress
- 2 Voice of Victory
- 1 Beza, the Bounding Spring

**Why these cards**
- **The shell:** It comes from Jeskai Control (76 recent lists). A 5-0 league list of that deck already ran 3 Resonating Lute and 3 Revelation, so the core is tested.
- **Inevitable Defeat:** It can't be countered, so it's a clean answer in counterspell mirrors. It's been in 28 lists in the last 90 days, almost all filed as "Rogue."
- **Lightning Helix over Burst Lightning:** The deck checker suggested Burst Lightning, but Helix is in 80% of Jeskai Control lists. Its 3 life matters against Prowess and Boros, which are the top of the field.

**The mana**
- **Black splash:** Black is only needed for Inevitable Defeat, which is an instant. That makes Great Hall (any color for instants and sorceries, for 1 life) a near-free black source. The deck has 10 black sources: 4 Great Hall, 2 Starting Town, and one each of Godless Shrine ×2, Watery Grave and Blood Crypt.
- **Color counts:** 19 white, 20 blue and 14 red sources, all at or above what real Jeskai Control lists run. The land checker passed with no warnings.
- **Life cost:** Shocklands, Starting Town and Great Hall all cost life. Against aggro, play your shocklands tapped when you can.
- **Odds:** You naturally draw Lute by turn 5 on the play 56.6% of the time, and Consult and Stock Up raise that. Drawing Lute plus Revelation or Defeat by turn 5 is about 37%. That's fine, because both payoffs can be cast without Lute; it only makes them faster.

**Sideboarding**
- **Prowess (20.8% of the field) and Boros Aggro:** Bring in Pyroclasm, Fire Magic and Beza. Take out Spell Snare and a Stock Up or Lute.
- **Landfall and Elementals:** Bring in Pyroclasm and Disdainful Stroke. Take out a Seam Rip.
- **Dimir Excruciator, Lessons and other control decks:** Bring in Duress, Negate, Voice of Victory and Disdainful Stroke. Take out Day of Judgment, Seam Rip and Get Lost. Voice of Victory stops them casting spells on your turn, which protects Lute and Revelation.
- **Graveyard-heavy decks:** Bring in Rest in Peace.

**What I couldn't verify**
- None of the Inevitable Defeat lists I found were broken out as their own archetype, so I couldn't compare this exact four-color mana against a proven list. The black-splash land count is my own judgment.
- The sideboard plans are reasoning from the card text, not tested results.

plan.thesis: Four-color Jeskai control splashing black: cheap counters, Helix and sweepers survive the early game while Consult/Stock Up dig for Resonating Lute. Once Lute lands, every land makes two mana of any color for spells, so Inevitable Defeat and Jeskai Revelation (often two per turn) bury the opponent, with Lute drawing extra cards off a full grip.

You draw 1+ engine (doubles land mana for instants/sorceries, fixes black) (4 in the deck), 1+ payoff spells (6 in the deck) by turn 5 in 37% of games (on the play, mulligans included). The 3 life matters against Prowess and Boros (the top of the meta), and with no creatures in the main deck it also adds reach to finish games. Burst Lightning gains no life, and Boomerang Basics isn't removal.

This is a control deck first, not a combo deck that has to assemble its pieces by turn 5. Revelation and Defeat are both castable off normal lands (10 black sources for Defeat counting Great Hall), and Lute only speeds them up. I'm also running 8 dig spells (Consult, Stock Up) that the raw odds don't count toward finding Lute. The real plan is to survive with 2-mana interaction and take over around turns 5-7.

results.prompt: Brew me a Standard deck built around Dáin's Company, Dwarven Mauler and Kíli the Resourceful.
results.text:
I built a Boros (red-white) Dwarf Equipment aggro deck. It's a **brew**: none of the three cards you named shows up in recent Standard results (0 lists in the last 90 days for each). The deck passed the legality check and the coach check with no notes.

**The plan:** Play two cheap Dwarves a turn starting on turn 1, then put Equipment on them. Dáin's Company finds more Dwarves or Equipment. Kíli draws a card when they enter, and once you control 3 artifacts or legendary permanents (its "storied" condition), Kíli makes your first equip each turn free. Burn spells and Mjölnir clear blockers, and the gear makes small Dwarves win combat.

**Main deck (60)**
- **Creatures (23):** 4 Dwarven Mauler, 4 Kíli the Resourceful, 4 Dáin's Company, 4 Thorin Oakenshield, 3 Giott, King of the Dwarves, 2 Dáin Ironfoot, 2 Fíli the Pathfinder
- **Equipment (8):** 4 Dwarven Mattock, 2 Lost Jitte, 2 Mjölnir, Hammer of Thor
- **Burn (6):** 4 Burst Lightning, 2 Lightning Helix
- **Lands (23):** 4 Sacred Foundry, 4 Inspiring Vantage, 4 Sunbillow Verge, 2 Sundown Pass, 2 The Lonely Mountain, 4 Mountain, 3 Plains

**Sideboard (15):** 2 Abrade, 2 Scorching Shot, 2 Torch the Tower, 2 Authority of the Consuls, 2 Dawn's Truce, 2 Shattered Acolyte, 2 Ghost Vacuum, 1 Thorin, Mountain-king

**Why these cards**
- **Dwarven Mauler:** A 2/1 for {R} that makes equips targeting it cost {2} less. Dwarven Mattock's equip {3} becomes {1} on it, and Lost Jitte's equip {1} becomes free.
- **Dáin's Company:** Looks at the top 4 cards for a Dwarf or Equipment. Every creature and every piece of gear in the deck is a hit. It also has lifelink while you control another Dwarf.
- **Kíli:** Most of your plays trigger its draw (once per turn). The storied condition comes up fast because Kíli, Thorin, Giott, Dáin Ironfoot, Fíli, Jitte and Mjölnir are all legendary, and Mattock, Jitte and Mjölnir are artifacts.
- **Dwarven Mattock:** Attaches itself to a Dwarf when it enters, giving +2/+2 and ward {1}, so you don't pay to equip it the first time.
- **Giott:** A double striker that lets you discard and draw whenever a Dwarf or Equipment enters. It's a strong carrier for gear.
- **Thorin Oakenshield:** A 3/2 trampler for 2. With storied active, your artifacts and creatures get ward {1}.
- **Mjölnir:** Deals 4 damage to a creature when it enters, doubles the damage of the creature carrying it, and costs only {1} to equip on your legendary red or white Dwarves (Kíli, Thorin, Giott, Dáin, Fíli).
- **Dáin Ironfoot and Fíli:** Extra reach at 3 and 4 mana. Dáin makes an Axe token and gives equipped attackers double strike. Fíli makes a 2/2 Dwarf token whenever a nontoken Dwarf enters.

**How often it comes together**
By turn 3 on the play, you see Kíli or Dáin's Company 75% of the time and an Equipment 75% of the time. You see both together 55% of the time, not counting mulligans. That 55% doesn't count Dáin's Company finding an Equipment for you, so the real rate is somewhat higher.

**Mana**
The lands are borrowed from real Boros lists. The deck has 20 red sources and 17 white; the gold two-drops need both colors early. I used only 2 Sundown Pass because it enters tapped in the early turns. The Lonely Mountain enters untapped once you have an Equipment, and later turns spare mana into 2/2 Dwarves (it costs {1} less per Equipment you control). 23 lands is in line with real Boros Aggro decks, which run about 23.4.

**Sideboarding against the main decks**
- **Prowess (21.7%) and Elementals (8%):** Bring in Abrade, Torch the Tower and Scorching Shot. Take out Fíli and Lightning Helix if you need room. Ghost Vacuum (also an artifact, so it counts toward storied) helps against their graveyard plans.
- **Selesnya Offense (13.5%) and Landfall (9.6%):** Bring in Scorching Shot for their big creatures. Authority of the Consuls makes their creatures enter tapped, so they can't block right away and haste creatures lose their surprise attack.
- **Lessons, 4C Control and Dimir Excruciator:** Bring in Dawn's Truce to protect your board from Day of Judgment and Slagstorm, plus Ghost Vacuum and Thorin, Mountain-king. Cut some burn.
- **Artifact or enchantment decks (Boros Weapons, Rest in Peace players):** Shattered Acolyte is a Dwarf with lifelink that can sacrifice itself to destroy an artifact or enchantment.

**What I couldn't check**
- These Dwarves have no tournament results, so the card counts are reasoned, not proven. The places I'd tune first are 2 vs. 4 Lost Jitte and 3 vs. 4 Giott.
- I didn't look up how Lessons, Selesnya, Landfall or the control decks are built. The plans above for those matchups go by deck name, plus their use of Ghost Vacuum, Slagstorm and Day of Judgment from the card lookups.

plan.thesis: Boros Dwarf-Equipment aggro: cheap Dwarves curve out, Dáin's Company digs for more Dwarves or gear, Kíli draws off every Dwarf/Equipment drop and makes equips free once storied (3 artifacts/legends), and Dwarven Mauler wears Mattocks/Jittes for cheap. Burn clears blockers and Mjölnir doubles as removal and a finisher on legendary Dwarves.

results.text:
I built this as **Orzhov Aristocrats (white-black)**, and it's a **brew**: no proven list exists for it. Each of your three cards shows up in only one recent tournament list.

**Main deck (60)**
- 4 Greedy Freebooter
- 3 The Sackville-Bagginses
- 4 Umbral Collar Zealot
- 4 Bloodghast
- 3 Voice of Victory
- 4 Tolls of War
- 1 Bartolomé del Presidio
- 3 Popular Egotist
- 2 Kambal, Profiteering Mayor
- 3 Vito, Fanatic of Aclazotz
- 2 Requiting Hex
- 3 Bitter Triumph
- 2 Get Lost
- **Lands (22):** 4 Godless Shrine, 4 Concealed Courtyard, 3 Shattered Sanctum, 3 Bleachbone Verge, 2 Starting Town, 4 Swamp, 2 Plains

**Sideboard (15)**
- 3 Seam Rip
- 3 Duress
- 2 Strategic Betrayal
- 2 Leyline of the Void
- 2 Deathmark
- 1 Requiting Hex
- 2 Pyrrhic Strike

**The plan**
Play cheap creatures that leave tokens behind when they go, and sacrifice them for value. Every sacrifice drains the opponent, which finishes off games that your early attackers start.

**Why these cards**
- **Umbral Collar Zealot** lets you sacrifice a creature or artifact for free (you surveil 1), as often as you like. That makes your death and sacrifice triggers happen whenever you want.
- **Greedy Freebooter** is the ideal thing to sacrifice. When it dies you scry 1 and get a Treasure. Sacrificing that Treasure for mana is sacrificing a token, so **The Sackville-Bagginses** makes the opponent lose 1 life. Sackville-Bagginses' own enter trigger also sacrifices something to draw a card and make another Treasure. It's legendary, so I run 3 copies instead of 4.
- **More tokens:**
  - **Tolls of War** makes a Clue when it enters, then a 1/1 Ally the first time you sacrifice something on your turn.
  - **Voice of Victory** makes two 1/1 Warriors each time it attacks, and they're sacrificed at end of turn. Those are two token sacrifices per attack. It also stops opponents from casting spells during your turn.
  - **Bloodghast** comes back from the graveyard every time you play a land, so you can sacrifice it again and again.
- **The payoffs:**
  - **Popular Egotist:** the opponent loses 1 and you gain 1 on every sacrifice.
  - **Vito:** your first sacrifice each turn gains 2 life, the second drains 2, and the third makes a 4/3 flyer.
  - **Kambal:** drains 1 whenever your tokens enter.
- **Removal:** Requiting Hex can use a -1/-1 counter on a Freebooter you were happy to lose anyway. Bitter Triumph and Get Lost are clean answers. I left out Erode because it gives the opponent a land, which helps the Landfall decks.
- **The coach's check:** it measured how often you have something to sacrifice, a sacrifice outlet and a drain card by turn 3. It had no concerns.

**Mana**
I copied the land setup from the Lifegain deck (72 recent lists), which is also white-black. That's 22 lands: dual lands, Shattered Sanctum, Bleachbone Verge and Starting Town. The deck has 22 black sources and 20 white sources. The deck checker passed it against real Lifegain lists with no warnings. The curve is very low (average mana value 2.13, with 24 two-drops), and Treasures act as extra mana.

**Sideboarding against the field**
- **Prowess (17.4%) and Boros or Gruul aggro:** bring in Seam Rip and the third Requiting Hex. Take out Kambal and Bartolomé.
- **Landfall (14.7%) and Selesnya Offense (8.1%):** bring in Deathmark (it kills green or white creatures), Seam Rip and Pyrrhic Strike. Take out Kambal and a Voice of Victory.
- **Lessons and 4C Control:** bring in Duress. Voice of Victory stays in, since it stops them casting spells on your turn. Take out Requiting Hex and Get Lost. Watch out for Day of Judgment: Bloodghast and Tolls of War help you rebuild after it.
- **Dimir Excruciator, Dimir Midrange and Reanimator:** bring in Strategic Betrayal and Leyline of the Void. Add Duress if they have key noncreature spells.

**What I couldn't verify**
None of these sacrifice cards show up in recent results, so I can't tell you how this does against the real meta. The card lines and odds hold up on paper, but it hasn't been tested. Pyrrhic Strike's blight cost needs a creature to put the counters on; I'm assuming you'll usually have a spare token. I deliberately left Clarion Conqueror out of the sideboard because it would shut off your own Zealot and Treasures.

plan.thesis: Orzhov aristocrats: cheap fodder that leaves tokens behind (Freebooter Treasures, Tolls of War Clues/Allies, Voice of Victory's mobilize Warriors, recurring Bloodghast) feeds free sac outlets, and every sacrifice drains through The Sackville-Bagginses, Popular Egotist, Vito and Kambal. Creatures beat down early, then the drain finishes.

- **Creatures (14):** 4 Gran-Gran, 4 Sokka, Bold Boomeranger, 3 Dragonfly Swarm, 3 Retriever Phoenix
- **Spells (26):** 4 Igneous Inspiration, 4 Combustion Technique, 4 Abandon Attachments, 4 Accumulate Wisdom, 3 Academic Dispute, 3 Fiery Impulse, 2 Boomerang Basics, 2 Firebending Lesson

results.text:
# Rakdos "Thud Shadow": Modern brew

## The plan
This deck pays its own life on purpose. Fetchlands, shocklands, Thoughtseize, Street Wraith cycling, Spoils of the Vault and Plunge into Darkness all lower your life. Death's Shadow is a 13/13 that gets -X/-X, where X is your life total, so every point you lose makes it bigger. At 4 life it's a 9/9. You can attack with it, or sacrifice it to Thud ("deals damage equal to the sacrificed creature's power to any target") for 1 mana and hit the opponent's face for 8–12 out of nowhere. Spoils and Plunge are both ways to lose life and ways to find whichever half of the combo you're missing.

## Decklist (60)
**Creatures (16)**
- 4 Death's Shadow
- 4 Street Wraith
- 3 Ragavan, Nimble Pilferer
- 3 Nethergoyf
- 2 Scourge of the Skyclaves

**Spells (26)**
- 4 Thud
- 4 Spoils of the Vault
- 3 Plunge into Darkness
- 4 Thoughtseize
- 4 Mishra's Bauble
- 3 Lightning Bolt
- 3 Unholy Heat
- 1 Fatal Push

**Lands (18)**
- 4 Bloodstained Mire
- 2 Marsh Flats
- 1 Arid Mesa
- 1 Polluted Delta
- 1 Verdant Catacombs
- 1 Wooded Foothills
- 2 Blood Crypt
- 2 Sulfurous Springs
- 3 Swamp
- 1 Mountain

**Sideboard (15)**
- 3 Leyline of the Void
- 2 Kolaghan's Command
- 2 Damping Sphere
- 2 Blood Moon
- 2 Collective Brutality
- 2 Terminate
- 1 Duress
- 1 Meltdown

## Why these cards
- **Spoils of the Vault** (1 mana, instant): you name a card, then reveal cards until you find it, losing 1 life for each other card revealed. That life loss feeds Shadow.
  - With Shadow already in play, name Thud. With Thud in hand, name Shadow.
  - **Warning:** it can kill you. With 4 copies of the named card, expect to reveal about 10 cards. Cast it at a healthy life total, and don't cast it below about 8 life unless it wins on the spot.
- **Plunge into Darkness** (2 mana, instant):
  - Its "pay X life, look at X cards, take one" mode digs for Thud or Shadow and shrinks your life at the end of the opponent's turn.
  - Its sacrifice mode gains 3 life per creature. That's an emergency reset if you've dropped too low, for example by sacrificing a Ragavan or Nethergoyf.
- **Scourge of the Skyclaves**: its power and toughness equal 20 minus the highest life total among players. It's a second big creature to Thud once both players are low. It's weaker when the opponent's life is still high, so there are only 2.
- **Street Wraith and Mishra's Bauble**: these are almost free cards that thin the deck, so 18 lands is enough. Wraith cycles for 2 life, which also grows Shadow.
- **Ragavan, Nethergoyf, Bolt, Unholy Heat and Thoughtseize**: this is the Death's Shadow archetype's proven support (the tool showed Thoughtseize ×4, Bolt ×4 and Heat ×4 in its list), so the deck can win normally when the combo doesn't come together.

**Odds:** with no mulligans, you'll see at least one of Shadow, Scourge or Spoils plus at least one Thud or Plunge by turn 4 on the play **63.1%** of the time. That number doesn't count the extra cards from Street Wraith, Bauble or Plunge's digging, so the real figure is higher.

## The mana
- There are 18 lands and the average mana value is 1.4.
- Every fetchland can find Blood Crypt, so all ten count as both black and red sources. Fetch for basics when you can, to stay safe from Blood Moon.
- Sulfurous Springs pings you for colored mana, which suits this deck.
- Black is the main color (Shadow, Spoils, Plunge, Thoughtseize). Red covers Thud, Bolt, Heat and Ragavan.

## Sideboarding against the field
The meta tool showed Energy 14.5%, Blink 14.4%, Prowess 9.8%, Affinity 8.6%, Domain Zoo 8.2%, Storm 4.9% and Goryo's Vengeance 3.3%.
- **Prowess, Energy and Zoo:** these decks attack your low life total. Bring in Terminate and Collective Brutality, which can drain 2 life back to you. Take out a Spoils and a Plunge, play Shadow less aggressively, and count on Plunge's sacrifice mode to gain life back.
- **Affinity:** bring in Kolaghan's Command, Meltdown and Terminate. Take out Thoughtseize.
- **Storm and Goryo's Vengeance:** bring in Duress and Damping Sphere against Storm, and Leyline of the Void against Goryo's. Take out removal.
- **Blink, Amulet Titan and Eldrazi:** bring in Blood Moon and Damping Sphere. Keep the hand disruption in.

## Label and caveats
**This is a brew.** No tournament list in the results runs Thud, Spoils or Plunge; all three show 0 lists in the last 90 days. I took the shell (discard, burn, Ragavan, Wraith, Bauble, fetches) from the Death's Shadow archetype data, but that data is based on **only one list**. Treat the land count and the exact numbers as a starting point, not tested results. The sideboard is my own choice for the current meta, not copied from any list.

We either attack with it or Thud it at the opponent's face for 8-12 damage out of nowhere, using Spoils/Plunge to find whichever half is missing.

# Grixis Buried Phoenix (Legacy brew)

**The plan:** Put Arclight Phoenixes into your graveyard, then cast three instants or sorceries in one turn so they come back at the beginning of combat. Buried Alive does the first job on its own: "Search your library for up to three creature cards, put them into your graveyard." That means all three can be Phoenixes. The fastest line is Dark Ritual, then Buried Alive, then any one-mana spell, which is three spells in one turn. That returns three 3/2 flying, hasty Phoenixes for 9 damage, possibly on turn 1 with Lotus Petal and usually by turn 2. Flow State and the cantrips (cheap spells that draw a card) restock your hand, and Force of Will protects the key turn.

**Main deck (60)**
- 4 Arclight Phoenix
- 4 Buried Alive
- 4 Faithless Looting
- 4 Dark Ritual
- 4 Lava Dart
- 2 Manamorphose
- 4 Flow State
- 4 Brainstorm
- 4 Ponder
- 4 Force of Will
- 3 Lotus Petal
- 2 Thoughtseize
- 1 Lightning Bolt
- 4 Polluted Delta
- 4 Bloodstained Mire
- 2 Scalding Tarn
- 2 Underground Sea
- 2 Volcanic Island

- 1 Swamp

**Sideboard (15)**

- 2 Force of Negation
- 2 Fatal Push
- 2 Chain of Vapor
- 2 Surgical Extraction
- 2 Abrade
- 2 Thoughtseize

**Why these cards**
- **Buried Alive:** It's both your tutor and your setup. You only need the one card, not a Phoenix plus a way to discard it. Faithless Looting is the second way to bin Phoenixes. You can discard one you drew, and its flashback gives you an extra spell on a later turn.
- **Dark Ritual:** It's an instant that adds BBB, so it pays for Buried Alive and also counts as one of your three spells.
- **Free or near-free spells:**
  - Lava Dart's flashback costs only "Sacrifice a Mountain." Volcanic Island and Badlands count as Mountains, so it's a free third spell.
  - Manamorphose costs 2 and gives back two mana plus a card, so it's a free spell when you have the mana.
  - Lotus Petal makes the turn-1 kill possible.
- **Flow State:** Once the graveyard has an instant and a sorcery (it almost always will), it picks two of your top three cards instead of one. That refills your hand after you spend it on a combo turn.
- **Two cards you might expect are missing:** I checked Entomb and Gitaxian Probe, and both are banned in Legacy.

**Odds (on the play, no mulligans):**
- 75% to have Buried Alive or Looting by turn 3.
- 49% to have Buried Alive itself by turn 3.
- 30% to have both a binning card and Dark Ritual by turn 2.

Brainstorm and Ponder push all of these numbers higher.

**The mana:** 16 lands, with the fetch lands and dual lands taken from the Reanimator shell. Every fetch can find every dual. The deck has 13 blue, 15 black and 12 red sources. The deck checker noted that Reanimator decks run about 18 black sources. That's fine here, because those decks are almost mono-black and this one needs three colors.

**Sideboarding against the most-played decks**
- **Dimir Tempo and Izzet Tempo (the two most common decks):** Bring in Pyroblast against their blue threats and counterspells. Fatal Push and Abrade also come in against Izzet. Take out Thoughtseize and Manamorphose.

- **Reanimator:** Bring in Surgical Extraction and Thoughtseize.

- **Graveyard hate:** Leyline of the Void shows up in a lot of decks (33% of results), including Tron, Ocelot Aggro, The Epic Storm and Oops All Spells. Chain of Vapor bounces it back to their hand, which makes them pay 4 mana to replay it, and it counts toward your three spells. Expect Surgical Extraction from tempo decks too. This hate is the deck's biggest weakness.

**Things to know:**
- This is a brew. Arclight Phoenix appears in 0 recent Legacy lists, so there's no tournament evidence that this beats the field.
- The mana base and interaction are borrowed from proven decks: Reanimator for the mana, and the blue tempo decks for Force of Will and the cantrips. Flow State shows up in 338 recent lists.
- The coach (an automated checker that measures how often the deck draws its combo pieces) passed the deck with no notes. The deck check also found no errors.
