I built a UR combo deck that turns your three cards into an infinite-damage loop with no other pieces needed. It's a **brew**: none of the three cards has shown up in any Vintage result in the last 90 days.

## The plan
You need three things: Goblin Welder on the battlefield without summoning sickness, Sewer-veillance Cam on the battlefield, and Legion Extruder in your graveyard (it also works with Cam and Extruder the other way round). Then you loop:
1. **Tap Welder:** sacrifice Cam and return Extruder at the same time. Cam's "leaves the battlefield" trigger untaps Welder. Extruder's "enters" trigger deals 2 damage to any target.
2. **Tap Welder again:** sacrifice Extruder and return Cam. Cam's "enters" trigger untaps Welder.
3. You're back where you started, 2 damage up. Repeat until the opponent is dead.

## Key cards
- **Getting a piece into the graveyard:**
  - Goblin Engineer (4): when it enters, it puts any artifact from your library straight into your graveyard.
  - Legion Extruder itself: {2}, tap, sacrifice another artifact (like Cam) to make a 3/3. That bins Cam, and you get a body too.
  - Cam itself: {3}{U}, sacrifice it to draw two.
  - Tinker and Transmute Artifact: sacrifice Cam and put Extruder onto the battlefield. That's 2 damage, and now Cam is in the graveyard.
- **Backup loop:** Goblin Engineer can run the same swap without Welder, but it costs {R} each time.
- **Finding Welder:** Imperial Recruiter (2) and Goblin Matron (2).
- **Finding Cam** (it costs 1): Trinket Mage, Urza's Saga's chapter III, and Tezzeret, Cruel Captain's −3. Whir of Invention and Fabricate can find either artifact.
- **Swiftfoot Boots, not Lightning Greaves:** Greaves gives shroud, which stops Cam's trigger from targeting your own Welder. Boots gives hexproof, which only stops opponents. Boots give Welder haste, so you can win the turn it comes down.
- **Protection and speed:** 4 Force of Will, Force of Negation, Mental Misstep, plus the restricted blue cards (Ancestral Recall, Time Walk, Brainstorm).

**Odds:** the coach measured about 50% of games having a Welder or Welder-finder, a Cam or Cam-finder, and an Extruder or Extruder-enabler by turn 4 on the play, mulligans included. I set turn 4 as the target because Welder normally has to survive a turn before it can tap. Turn 3 measured only about 40% with an earlier version of the list. Adding the second Goblin Matron is what got turn 4 over the line.

## Mana
- **15 lands:** 4 Volcanic Island, 6 fetchlands, 1 Island, 1 Mountain, Urza's Saga, Strip Mine and Ancient Tomb.
- **9 fast-mana artifacts:** Black Lotus, all five Moxen, Sol Ring, Mana Crypt and Mana Vault. The off-colour Moxen are still useful as artifacts to sacrifice.
- The deck has 12 blue and 10 red sources. That's a bit fewer blue sources than real Tinker lists (about 14), because this is a two-colour deck.
- The checker suggests about 17.5 lands, but real Tinker lists run about 14, so 15 plus the fast mana is fine.

## Sideboarding
| Opponent | Bring in |
|---|---|
| Lurrus Control / Lurrus PO / Paradoxical Outcome (about 45% of the field) | Pyroblast, Flusterstorm ×2, Mindbreak Trap ×2 |
| Raker Shops / Sphere Shops (21%) | Abrade ×2, Fiery Confluence ×2, Pithing Needle (on Walking Ballista or Tezzeret) |
| Dredge (7%) | Tormod's Crypt ×2, Soul-Guide Lantern, Grafdigger's Cage, Pithing Needle (on Bazaar) |
| Mono-White Initiative | Kozilek's Return, Fiery Confluence ×2, Abrade ×2 |
| Oath | Grafdigger's Cage. Your own Welders and Engineers also stop Oath from triggering. |

Cut Trinket Mage, Tezzeret, Transmute Artifact and one Recruiter first.

## Things I couldn't verify
- Tezzeret's starting loyalty wasn't in the card text I got, so check that it can use its −3 right away.
- Shops' Sphere effects and artifact removal hit this deck hard. That matchup is the biggest risk.

plan.thesis: With Sewer-veillance Cam on the battlefield and Legion Extruder in the graveyard (or the other way around), Goblin Welder swaps them back and forth: Cam leaving or entering untaps Welder each time and every Extruder entry deals 2 damage, so the loop deals infinite damage. Welder has to lose summoning sickness (or wear Swiftfoot Boots), so the realistic kill turn is 4, with Moxen, Force of Will and the restricted blue cards supplying speed and protection.

results.prompt: Brew me a Pauper deck built around Ardent Recruit, Search Party Captain and Springleaf Drum.
results.text:
I built a mono-white artifact weenie deck. The three cards you asked for drive it: Springleaf Drum, Ardent Recruit and Search Party Captain. The deck checks out as legal and the coach accepted it. **Label: brew.** None of your three cards has a winning tournament list right now, so this is not a copy of a proven deck. I borrowed the sideboard approach from the popular Mono-White Aggro deck and some artifact pieces from the Glintblade and Synthesizer decks.

**Main deck (60)**
- 4 Ardent Recruit
- 4 Ornithopter
- 4 Thraben Inspector
- 3 Novice Inspector
- 4 Court Homunculus
- 4 Glint Hawk
- 2 Kor Skyfisher
- 4 Auriok Sunchaser
- 4 Search Party Captain
- 4 Springleaf Drum
- 4 Dispatch
- 2 Journey to Nowhere
- 4 Ancient Den
- 13 Plains

**Sideboard (15)**
- 3 Dust to Dust
- 3 Prismatic Strands
- 2 Journey to Nowhere
- 2 Holy Light
- 2 Relic of Progenitus
- 2 Thraben Charm
- 1 Destroy Evil

**The plan**
Many of your cards count "metalcraft," which turns on when you control three or more artifacts. Cheap artifacts get you there fast: Ornithopter (free), Springleaf Drum, Ancient Den (an artifact land), Court Homunculus and the Clue tokens from the two Inspectors. Then Ardent Recruit is a 3/3 for one mana, Auriok Sunchaser is a 3/3 flier for two, and Dispatch exiles a creature for one mana. Once you're attacking with a wide board, Search Party Captain costs W or nothing and draws a card.

**Why these cards**
- **Springleaf Drum:** you can tap a creature that just came into play to pay for it, so turn-one creatures and Ornithopter become extra mana. It's also an easy artifact for metalcraft.
- **Glint Hawk and Kor Skyfisher:** both must return a card you control to your hand. Bouncing Drum, Ornithopter or an Inspector costs you almost nothing, and replaying an Inspector makes another Clue.
- **Search Party Captain:** costs 1 less for each creature you attacked with. With 27 one-drops and 4 free Ornithopters, it's often cheap on turns 3–4. It's the deck's card advantage, not something you need early.
- **Odds:** the coach found you'll have three artifacts (Clues counted) plus a metalcraft card by turn 3 in at least 60% of games, mulligans included. That's the threshold it requires. Earlier drafts were at 51–52%, which is why I cut two Kor Skyfishers for three Novice Inspectors.

**The mana**
17 lands (4 Ancient Den, 13 Plains) plus 4 Drums. The checker suggested about 19 lands, which is what Mono-White Aggro lists play. I kept fewer because the average card cost is only 1.37, the Drums produce mana, and the only expensive card is the Captain, which gets cheaper. If you flood, cut a Plains for a fourth Kor Skyfisher. If you get stuck on lands, add the 18th land.

**Sideboarding against the current field**
- **Affinity (6.6% of the field), Synthesizer and Glintblade:** bring in Dust to Dust (exiles two artifacts) and Destroy Evil. Take out the Court Homunculi.
- **Madness (16.6%) and Terror (13.9%):** bring in Relic of Progenitus, which also counts toward metalcraft, plus Journey to Nowhere. Take out Ornithopters.
- **Elves (6.4%), Faeries and Mono-Red Rally:** bring in Holy Light, Prismatic Strands and Thraben Charm. Holy Light gives non-white creatures -1/-1, so it kills your own Ornithopters. Take those out first.
- **Gates and Jeskai Control:** Thraben Charm destroys enchantments. Prismatic Strands helps against sweepers that deal damage.

**What I couldn't verify**
- Ardent Recruit, Search Party Captain, Auriok Sunchaser, Court Homunculus and Dispatch have 0 tournament lists in the last 90 days. Springleaf Drum has 7. How these cards perform against the current field is untested.
- The card database lists Search Party Captain as a 2/2. Check your printing.
- The Drum can make any color, so a red splash for Galvanic Blast is possible. I left it out to keep the mana consistent, and I haven't tested it.

plan.thesis: Mono-white artifact weenie: cheap artifacts (Ornithopter, Springleaf Drum, Ancient Den, Clues from the Inspectors, Court Homunculus) turn on metalcraft so Ardent Recruit and Auriok Sunchaser hit as 3/3s for one and two mana, while Springleaf Drum turns summoning-sick creatures into mana. Search Party Captain is the refuel top end, cast for W or free after a wide attack, rather than a piece the deck needs by turn 3.

results.prompt: Brew me a Pauper deck built around Aurora Eidolon, Sandstorm Eidolon and Spirit Mascot.
results.text:
I built a Boros (red-white) brew around your three cards: **Boros Spirit Recursion**, 60 cards plus a 15-card sideboard. It's legal in Pauper and the checker accepted it.

**The plan.** Aurora Eidolon and Sandstorm Eidolon are 4-mana 2/2s that come back from your graveyard to your hand whenever you cast a multicolored spell. That's why this list has 19 red-white spells. You can use them freely: sacrifice Sandstorm so a blocker can't block, sacrifice Aurora to prevent 3 damage, or discard them to Faithless Looting. Then cast your next red-white spell and get them back. Spirit Mascot gets a +1/+1 counter whenever one or more cards leave your graveyard. Rebuying an Eidolon, or casting any flashback card, grows it. You win by going wide and finishing with Rally the Peasants after Sandstorm sacrifices clear the blockers.

**Deck**
- **Creatures (22):** 4 Boros Recruit, 4 Spirit Mascot, 4 Dog Walker, 4 Skyknight Legionnaire, 3 Aurora Eidolon, 3 Sandstorm Eidolon
- **Spells (20):** 4 Faithless Looting, 4 Lightning Bolt, 3 Battle Screech, 3 Fire at Will, 3 Rally the Peasants, 3 Prismatic Strands
- **Lands (18):** 3 Boros Garrison, 2 Wind-Scarred Crag, 2 Thriving Heath, 6 Plains, 5 Mountain

**Sideboard (15):** 3 Electrickery, 3 Red Elemental Blast, 2 Pyroblast, 3 Dust to Dust, 2 Thraben Charm, 2 Gorilla Shaman

**Why these cards**
- **Spells that bring the Eidolons back:**
  - Boros Recruit (a 1-mana hybrid card, so it's both red and white)
  - Spirit Mascot
  - Dog Walker, but only when cast face up for {R}{W}. Cast face down through disguise it's colorless and won't bring anything back.
  - Skyknight Legionnaire (flying, haste)
  - Fire at Will (hybrid instant, 3 damage split among attacking or blocking creatures)

  I searched for other playable red-white multicolored cards. Lightning Helix, Boros Charm and Boros Swiftblade are all **not legal** in Pauper. Arrows of Justice is also not legal.
- **Cards that grow Spirit Mascot:** Faithless Looting, Rally the Peasants, Battle Screech and Prismatic Strands all have flashback, so casting them from the graveyard gives Mascot a counter. Looting is also how you put Eidolons in the graveyard early.
- **Borrowed from the Boros Aggro decks that show up in results:** Bolt, Strands, Rally, Screech and Looting. Every white creature in this deck can help pay Screech's and Strands' flashback costs.

**The mana.** 18 lands, with 13 white sources and 12 red. The checker found no warnings. Real Boros Aggro lists run about 19 lands and 16 white sources. I went a little lower because there are no 5-drops and Looting smooths out your draws. If you keep getting stuck on WW for Battle Screech, swap a Mountain for a Plains.

**Sideboarding**
- **Madness (16%) and Mono-Red Rally:** Prismatic Strands already shuts down a turn of their burn. Bring in Electrickery for their small creatures.
- **Terror (13.5%) and Faeries:** +3 Red Elemental Blast, +2 Pyroblast, +Electrickery against Faeries. Take out Fire at Will (a weak removal spell against them) and a Strands.
- **Affinity:** +3 Dust to Dust, +2 Gorilla Shaman.
- **Golgari Gardens and other graveyard or enchantment decks:** Thraben Charm. Its graveyard-exile mode also triggers your own Mascot if it hits your graveyard.
- **Elves and Mono-White Aggro:** Electrickery.

**Label: brew.** Nobody in recent results plays any of your three cards (0 lists in the last 90 days). I borrowed the shell and mana from Boros Aggro, but the engine is new.

**Honest odds and caveats**
- The coach found you'll have an Eidolon (or a Looting to dig for one) plus a red-white spell by turn 5 often enough.
- I first included Mascot as a required piece by turn 4. That combination came together in only about 33% of games, so treat a huge Mascot as a bonus, not the plan.
- The Eidolons are weak cards by themselves. This deck will probably be weaker than the top meta decks.
- The coach noted the deck has little card draw. I left it that way, because getting Eidolons back over and over, plus the flashback cards and Garrison, is the deck's card advantage.
- I didn't test how the deck actually plays against the meta.

plan.thesis: Boros aggro where Aurora and Sandstorm Eidolon are recursive 4-drops: sacrifice them for a fog or to stop a blocker, or discard them to Faithless Looting, then rebuy them with any of the red-white spells, while Spirit Mascot grows every time an Eidolon or a flashback card leaves the graveyard. Win by going wide with Battle Screech, Skyknights and a big Mascot, then finishing with Rally the Peasants plus Sandstorm sacrifices to clear blockers.

pieces.role: recursive payoff (or Looting to find/discard it)

notes.message: card advantage: this deck has 4; most midrange decks in recent pauper results have 12-22 (2243 lists). Fewer than 9 in 10 of them: add some, or say why this deck needs fewer.

responses.response: This is an aggro deck, not midrange, and its card advantage doesn't come from draw spells. Each Eidolon comes back to hand from the graveyard over and over (19 red-white spells rebuy them). Battle Screech and Rally have flashback, Faithless Looting turns extra lands into Eidolons in the graveyard, and Boros Garrison is a land that's worth two. Adding draw spells would mean cutting the threats the Eidolon loop needs.

results.prompt: Brew me a Premodern deck built around Living Death.
results.text:
I built a black-green Living Death brew for Premodern. Here's the list.

**Main deck (60)**
- **Spells:** 4 Living Death, 4 Buried Alive, 4 Dark Ritual, 3 Duress, 2 Cabal Therapy, 2 Exhume
- **Creatures:** 4 Putrid Imp, 4 Twisted Abomination, 3 Krosan Tusker, 2 Wirewood Guardian, 2 Nekrataal, 1 Bone Shredder, 1 Visara the Dreadful, 1 Deranged Hermit, 1 Uktabi Orangutan, 1 Gravedigger
- **Lands:** 11 Swamp, 4 Forest, 4 Llanowar Wastes, 2 Tainted Wood

**Sideboard (15):** 3 Smother, 3 Naturalize, 2 Engineered Plague, 2 Pernicious Deed, 2 Diabolic Edict, 2 Tormod's Crypt, 1 Withered Wretch

**The plan**
Fill your graveyard with big creatures and creatures that kill things when they enter. Then cast Living Death: it exiles every creature card from both graveyards, has both players sacrifice their creatures, then puts the exiled cards onto the battlefield. Their board dies and your 6/5s and 6/6s come back. Dark Ritual can make it a turn-3 play. For example: turn 2, Ritual into Buried Alive; turn 3, Ritual into Living Death.

**Why these cards**
- **Getting creatures into the graveyard:**
  - **Buried Alive** puts any three creatures there for 3 mana.
  - **The cyclers** double as land searches. Twisted Abomination (Swampcycling {2}, 5/3 that regenerates) and Wirewood Guardian (Forestcycling {2}, 6/6) fetch a land. Krosan Tusker (cycling {2}{G}, 6/5) finds a basic land and draws a card. You can cycle them at the end of your opponent's turn.
  - **Putrid Imp** lets you discard a card at no mana cost, so you can dump fatties from your hand.
- **Creatures that are better coming back:**
  - **Nekrataal and Bone Shredder** each destroy a nonblack creature when they enter.
  - **Visara** destroys a creature each time she taps.
  - **Deranged Hermit** brings four squirrels.
  - **Uktabi Orangutan** destroys an artifact.
  - **Gravedigger** returns a creature to your hand. Living Death has just put your old board into the graveyard, so there will be something to pick up.
- **Backup and protection:** 2 Exhume give you a cheap second way to bring a creature back. Duress and Cabal Therapy strip counterspells and removal before your big turn.
- **Odds** (on the play, no mulligans): by turn 4 you have about a 53% chance to have drawn Living Death and 68% to have Living Death or Exhume. You'll almost always have something to fill the graveyard (97.5%), and both together come to 66%.

**The mana**
21 lands with 17 black sources and 10 green. The 9 landcyclers and cyclers work as extra lands, which is why I stopped at 21. The checker compared this to the BG Survival decks I borrowed the land setup from, which run about 18.6 green sources. I kept green low on purpose: this deck is mostly black (Living Death needs BB, plus Ritual, Duress, Therapy and Imp). Green is mainly for Tusker's cycling, and Wirewood Guardian finds Forests when you need them.

**Sideboarding against the current field**
- **Tormod's Crypt is the biggest threat.** It shows up in about 43% of recent lists, including Sligh, Goblins and Zoo. Your discard spells can't take it once it's on the battlefield, so bring in Naturalize to destroy it before you go for Living Death. Also lean on Exhume and keep cycling at instant speed, so they have fewer good windows to use it.
- **Stiflenought (15%, the most-played deck):** bring in Diabolic Edict and Naturalize. A Phyrexian Dreadnought that comes back with Living Death has to sacrifice 12 power of creatures or die, so their graveyard working against them is fine.
- **Sligh and Goblins:** bring in Smother and Engineered Plague, and take out the Exhumes.
- **Enchantress:** bring in Pernicious Deed and Naturalize.
- **Opposing graveyard decks (Reanimator, Hermit Druid, Replenish):** bring in Tormod's Crypt and Withered Wretch. Crypt targets one player's graveyard, so it doesn't hurt you.

**Label and caveats**
This is a **brew**. Living Death has appeared in only about 7 recent lists, mostly as a single copy in BG Survival, so no proven version exists. I took only the land setup and sideboard ideas from BG Survival. Living Death works for both players, so check their graveyard before you cast it. Your Nekrataals and Bone Shredder help when you get that wrong. Nekrataal, Wirewood Guardian and Gravedigger had no recent tournament results, so their strength here is untested.

plan.thesis: Fill the graveyard with fatties and ETB-removal creatures via Buried Alive, landcyclers/cyclers and Putrid Imp discards, then cast Living Death (Dark Ritual accelerates it to turn 3-4) to wipe the opponent's board and return a bigger army. Exhume is a cheap backup reanimation and Duress/Cabal Therapy protect the key turn.

responses.response: This deck is black-first (Living Death BB, Dark Ritual, Buried Alive, Duress, Therapy, Imp), unlike green-first BG Survival. Green is only needed for Krosan Tusker cycling and the odd hard-cast, and Wirewood Guardian forestcycling finds Forests on demand.
